body: Uncapped Paris FC forward Pablo Pagis was surprisingly summoned by France on Friday for Nations League matches against Turkey and Italy.

Pagis, 23, made the 23-man list after Paris Saint-Germain’s Maghnes Akliouche was ruled out by a calf injury. France coach Zinedine Zidane said Pagis has an “interesting” and “different profile” that he wants to assess.

Pagis joined Paris FC in the summer after Lorient stay in Ligue 1 following promotion the previous season. Last season Pagis, who can play across the front line, scored 10 goals in Ligue 1 and has two this campaign. Paris FC are currently fourth in the league, with former Chelsea manager Liam Rosenior making positive return to French football.
France tops their Nations league group with 10 points from four games and travel to Italy on 12 November before hosting Turkey three days later.

articles.title: How Gotham FC re-tooled for another NWSL title run – this time as favorites
articles.summary: After two titles won as the lowest seed in the playoffs, the New Jersey club sought consistency in 2026. It’s arrived, but what’s next? By the time Gotham FC had won their second NWSL Championship in three seasons, Yael Averbuch West had already determined what was going to change.
body: Some of that is the nature of her job; the general manager of a perennial contender can’t rest on laurels. Before every postseason, Gotham finalize tough looming personnel decisions, assessing the roster and staff alike with clear eyes.

“I think psychologically, this is just really important,” Averbuch West told the Guardian. “Really, we knew what we needed to do. For us, it’s this continuous evolution of how we always look to improve. There’s nothing that’s ever safe from review.”

For all of their recent postseason success, with championships won as the lowest seed in 2023 and 2025, Gotham had never finished higher than third in any of their 17 seasons in NWSL or WPS. That trend was finally bucked in 2026, capped with last weekend’s capture of the NWSL Shield. But Averbuch West, alongside head coach Juan Carlos Amorós, wanted more consistency.

articles.title: Player-coach rift report will only galvanise England - George
articles.summary: England hooker Jamie George says the squad are "really upset" by a newspaper article claiming the end of their summer tour was marked by player unrest over Steve Borthwick's leadership.
body: A report in the Times, external says unhappy players wanted summit talks with Borthwick and Rugby Football Union chief executive Bill Sweeney in Argentina in July.

It alleges there are disagreements among Borthwick's wider coaching group, which has been subject to frequent change in his nearly four years in charge, and concerns over the head coach's man-management skills.
England meet Australia in the Nations Championship on Sunday at Allianz Stadium in Twickenham, with George querying the timing of the article as well as its contents.
The Saracens hooker, who was made England captain by Borthwick in 2024 before the role passed to Maro Itoje 12 months later, said that he did not recognise the situation described by the article.

articles.summary: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! For the FA Cup, the early rounds are the juice. The first round proper to be played out over the long weekend is looking, well, proper. And on Saturday at 3pm GMT, a proper time, 31 ties will kick off. No VAR, either.
body: Mansfield v Macclesfield In January, Macclesfield achieved the greatest shock in the competition’s history, knocking out the holders, Crystal Palace, in the third round. John Rooney’s National League North team head through the Pennines to face soundalikes Mansfield. Those from Macclesfield often find themselves having to correct others on coming from the Cheshire town rather than the one in Nottinghamshire. Macclesfield are such a modern club these days they have a sporting director in Keith Curle, a former Stags manager. Curle and current Mansfield boss Nigel Clough were England teammates at Euro 92, of which the less said the better.

Bradford City v Marine Merseyside’s most authentic, proper football club? Neither Everton nor Liverpool can compete with Crosby’s Marine. When modern football gets too much, the temptation to savour a pie and pint at Rossett Park, the club of Roly Howard, legendary manager for 33 years, becomes strong. On Saturday, Marine travel to Bradford City, on something of a slide since Graham Alexander de-camped to manage Preston.

articles.title: England players ‘fight to protect’ Steve Borthwick and deny rumours of rift
articles.summary: Team meet to discuss Times article on squad disharmony. Jamie George says criticism will get best from England. England’s senior players have circled the wagons around Steve Borthwick and denied he oversaw a toxic environment over the summer, insisting they will “fight to protect” the under-fire…
body: Jamie George, who captained the side for England’s three summer Tests, and the returning skipper, Maro Itoje, called a squad meeting on Friday morning to discuss an article in the Times that portrays a group of players fed up with Borthwick’s man management skills. The article goes on to say that Ellis Genge clashed with Borthwick, and that senior players sought clear-the-air talks with the head coach and wanted the Rugby Football Union chief executive, Bill Sweeney, present.

Borthwick insisted he doesn’t “recognise it as an accurate reflection” but chose not to engage with the accusations further, claiming “there’s nothing I need to respond to in there”, leaving his senior players to spring to his defence and insist he has not lost the faith of the squad. George conceded that the leadership group did have a virtual meeting with Borthwick in the aftermath of the summer tour to address ways to improve the environment but disputed suggestions it had become toxic. George also believes the fallout will boost England as they return to Twickenham on the back of five defeats in their past seven matches.

articles.title: Scotland come full circle for another crack at All Blacks
articles.summary: Sione Tuipulotu and Scotland have the chance to end one of sport's longest-standing hoodoos against New Zealand on Saturday, writes Andy Burke.
body: As Scotland prepare for their latest attempt at busting one of sport's longest standing hoodoos against the All Blacks on Saturday, it is worth reflecting on the journey this team has been on since their last tilt 12 months ago.

That match, in which Scotland fell 17-0 down, roared back to 17-17 all, only to succumb to the sorcery of Damien McKenzie late in the game, was another experience to file in Scottish rugby's bulging folder marked 'Ones That Got Away'.

It was a bitter disappointment, but worse was to follow when a 21-0 lead against Argentina spiralled into a nightmarish defeat that led to serious questions around the future of head coach Gregor Townsend.
The heat was turned up further still by a dispiriting loss to Italy in Rome to kick off this year's Six Nations. Since then, Scotland have flipped the narrative.

articles.title: George: England players hurt by 'shocking' report of rift with Borthwick
articles.summary: Jamie George says England's players were "hurt" by a newspaper report of a rift with head coach Steve Borthwick in the summer, calling the timing of the article "shocking" ahead of Sunday's Nations Championship clash with Australia.
body: The Times reported that some England players lost faith in Borthwick during a summer campaign with included a 45-21 defeat to world champions South Africa and a nervy win over Argentina.

It is alleged players objected to Borthwick's treatment of them, that he was involved in a training ground bust-up with Ellis Genge and that they wanted RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney - who this week unequivocally backed the head coach - to listen to their gripes.

Speaking to Sky Sports News on Friday, hooker George, captain for the July tour with Maro Itoje rested and named in the starting XV to face the Wallabies this weekend, says the squad addressed the article and will use it to "galavanise" them.

The 36-year-old, who insisted England are "all massively behind Steve in every way possible" said: "I'm really disappointed with the article that's been written. There's not a huge amount of truth to any of it, really.

articles.title: Is Palmer's England career over under Tuchel?
articles.summary: Cole Palmer faces a fight to save his England career after he was excluded from Thomas Tuchel's latest squad, says chief football writer Phil McNulty.
body: Thomas Tuchel's brutal assessment of Cole Palmer's exclusion from England's latest squad made it crystal clear Chelsea's gifted playmaker faces a fight to save his international career under the German head coach.
"He misses too many opportunities to impress" was Tuchel's blunt explanation for Palmer's absence, after the 24-year-old withdrew the previous England camp citing a minor injury.
Tuchel's message was so stark, so pointed, that Palmer must now be wondering when he will get another opportunity to impress.

And, to make it even more chastening, Tuchel took his decision after receiving assurances that Palmer was fully fit and available for selection for England's upcoming Nations League games - at home to Croatia then against World Cup holders Spain in Madrid.

articles.title: Carrick: 'Not impossible' Man Utd can achieve Ferguson success again
articles.summary: Michael Carrick believes Manchester United can reach the heights achieved under Sir Alex Ferguson but is not expecting the same level of patience.
body: Friday marks 40 years since Ferguson was appointed United manager on November 6, 1986. It is an anniversary that comes at a particularly significant moment for the club, with Carrick's position in charge still facing intense scrutiny.

United's dramatic 3-2 comeback victory over Roma in midweek offered Carrick some much-needed breathing space after a nine-game winless run, but Sunday's Premier League clash against Aston Villa, live on Sky, represents another significant test.
The timing of Ferguson's anniversary also provides an opportunity to reflect on the scale of the task facing United.

Ferguson inherited a club that had not won the league title since 1967 and needed almost seven years to deliver its first championship under him. What followed was an unprecedented period of success, including 13 Premier League titles and two Champions League crowns.

articles.title: Examining Houston Astros GM Randy Flores' connections to three managerial candidates
articles.summary: New Houston Astros GM Randy Flores wants to hire a manager quickly, so we examined some candidates to see how closely they're connected to the man in charge.
body: Randy Flores ' first task as Houston Astros general manager is to find a manager to replace Joe Espada. At Flores' introductory press conference Monday, he said that move was a priority, and this week a source confirmed to the Houston Chronicle's Matt Kawahara that Flores would interview his former teammate Albert Pujols for the job.

Flores was a star pitcher in college at USC and lasted eight years in the big leagues as a reliever before spending the past 11 seasons in the St. Louis Cardinals' front office, so he has plenty of connections throughout the game. Not coincidentally, Flores shared a clubhouse with Pujols for five seasons in St. Louis. For those interested in connecting dots, a couple other Flores' ties besides Pujols also have been mentioned as potential candidates to become the next Astros' manager.

articles.title: Miami Carol City football fights playoff ban with emergency injunction
articles.summary: Attorneys have filed for an emergency injunction on behalf of several Carol City football players and parents in Miami Circuit Court, according to former Miami Herald reporter Susan Miller Degnan.
body: The fight also resulted in restrictive probation for the football program, as well as 15 players receiving suspensions ranging from one game to the remainder of season.

Carol City appealed the postseason ban, and the FHSAA denied the appeal on Nov. 1. Now on Nov. 6, just hours before the playoff bracket release show is scheduled, the court has set a hearing on the matter.

"I have tremendous respect for the FHSAA," said attorney Jason Setchen in a post on X. "But I think that what they did to Miami Carol City Football by imposing a post season ban on the entire team, which includes many kids who did nothing wrong, is overreaching and unfair."

Coffey Burlington and Setchen filed the emergency injunction on Wednesday, Nov. 4. In the filing, the plaintiffs ask for judicial intervention to stop the FHSAA from "punishing promising high school football players for something they did not do."
